diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\nodes(\Omega)$ denote the set of interior vertices in $\tria$.

issues.failure_explanation: E is defined only at interior vertices. Its values at boundary vertices (zero, to land in S_0^1) are never specified. The proof of the first estimate bounds |v_h(j)-Ev_h(j)| by the max-min spread over the vertex patch, which is valid only for interior j. The right-hand side also sums only over interior faces. For T touching the boundary this is false. Take a continuous piecewise-affine w with boundary-vertex values alternating +c,-c, so that it vanishes at all boundary-face midpoints. Then w is in V_h and every jump vanishes. The right-hand side is 0, yet w-Ew is nonzero at boundary vertices because Ew is forced to be 0 there. The estimate (Enrichment) as stated, and the derived estimate (Enrichment2), therefore fail or are unproved on boundary elements.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define E at boundary vertices (zero). Include boundary faces in the sums, with jump equal to the trace of the tangential gradient. Prove the corresponding nodal bound using the zero face-mean (CR boundary condition). Extend the bubble-function arguments to boundary faces using v in W_0^{1,1}.
issues.overall_effect: The companion stability bound is used in Steps 1-3 of the main proof and in the interpolation estimate. Both are unproved for elements adjacent to the boundary, so the main theorem and the conforming a priori estimate are not fully established.
issues.title: Enrichment estimate ignores boundary vertices and boundary faces
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained extension of the lemma and its bubble arguments to boundary faces. The method and all conclusions survive, but it needs a new nontrivial argument rather than a one-line fix.

issues.failure_explanation: (i) Iterating the shift-change along the chain from T to T_+(gamma) produces error terms delta*|F(grad v_h(T_j)) - F(grad v_h(T_{j+1}))|^2. These are jumps of grad_h v_h, not of grad_h e_h, so they are not the quantity on the left-hand side and cannot be absorbed. (ii) In Case 2 the equivalence of phi_{|grad v_h(T_+)|}(|[[grad e_h]]|) with (phi_{|grad v_h(T_+)|})^*(|[[A(grad e_h)·nu]]|) invokes Prop. (Udal). That result requires the shift to equal the gradient inside A. Here A is evaluated at grad e_h while the shift is grad v_h(T_+). The equivalence is false in general. Example: p=4, shift 0, |a|=10, |a-b|=1 gives (|A(a)-A(b)|)^{4/3} of order 10^2.7 versus |a-b|^4 = 1. Moreover A(grad e_h) is not A(grad v_h)-A(grad u_h), because A is nonlinear. Hence (Enrichment2) with its phi_{|grad_h v_h|}(|grad_h(e_h - v)|) and divergence terms is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the control of the E-defect jump terms with correct shifts. Use shifts constant on patches, keep the shift-change error terms as jumps of grad_h v_h, and bound those separately (e.g. by the Case 1/2 machinery of the main proof). Use the proper shifted A (or A(grad u_h)) in the normal-jump argument. Restate the lemma with the extra terms and adapt the uses.
issues.overall_effect: Steps 1-3 of the main proof use (Enrichment2) (with v=0). The interpolation estimate of Theorem ApproxProperties also uses it. Their validity, and that of the conforming estimate, rests on an unproved companion estimate.
issues.title: Shift-change and shifted-duality equivalences applied with mismatched shifts in the proof of (Enrichment2)
issues.why_classification: A supported repair exists that stays within the same architecture: reuse the jump estimates already developed for v_h and adjust the lemma statement and its uses. It still needs a contained new argument and a modified lemma, so it is not minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and Jensen's inequality, we conclude for all piece-wise constant functions $\chi_\tria \in \mathbb{P}_0(\tria;\mathbb{R}^d)$ that

issues.failure_explanation: The step int_T phi_{|grad u|}(|Pi_0(grad u - chi)|) <= int_T phi_{|grad u|}(|grad u - chi|) is attributed to Jensen's inequality. Here the convex function phi_{|grad u(x)|} depends on x through the shift, which is not constant on T. Jensen applies only to a fixed convex function, so phi_{a}(avg g) <= avg phi_a(g) does not give the stated inequality when the shift varies. For example, the average of g can be large where the shift is small. The estimate is not justified as written. It would hold after first switching to the constant shift |chi_T| via the equivalence of Prop. (Distances).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the variable shift |grad u| by the piecewise-constant shift |chi_T| using the equivalence |F(P)-F(Q)|^2 ~ phi_{|Q|}(|P-Q|) with Q=chi_T. Then apply Jensen elementwise with constant shift and convert back.
issues.overall_effect: The bound of the non-conforming interpolation error by min_chi ||F(grad u) - chi||^2 is not justified as written. It is used in Theorem Apriori and in the proofs of Theorems ApproxProperties and AprioriConf.
issues.title: Jensen's inequality used with an x-dependent shift in the interpolation estimate (approxInc)
